newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh opposition party boycotts parliament.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh opposition party boycotts parliament.

text.p: The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) began boycotting parliament on Sunday, flashing signals that the country's newly-found political stability could soon be in danger.

"It is not possible for us to be in the House or participate in its proceedings because they are meaningless," BNP deputy leader Professor Badruddoza Chowdhury told reporters after handing a memorandum to Speaker Humayun Rasheed Chowdhury.
The memorandum contained decisions by a BNP meeting, headed by party chief Begum Khaleda Zia, a former prime minister.
It said: "BNP legislators will abstain from attending parliament until its grievances, conveyed to the Speaker, are redressed."
"We have made our points...and we will return to the House only after they are resolved," BNP's Chowdhury said.

The BNP said in the memorandum that the ruling Awami League had "turned parliament into a redundant body by obstructing the opposition from making their rightful observations on matters of national interest.

"We are not even allowed to discuss deteriorating law and order, or matters of serious concern like the water-sharing problem with India, giving India a proposed land transit through Bangladesh and importing power from that country.

"People are being misled by false, provocative and motivated statements by ministers and treasury bench MPs, which are broadcast over state-run television which itself is playing the voice of the government only."
The BNP's boycott decision has confirmed that an appeal by Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina for a consensus over major issues had fallen on deaf ears, Awami leader Suranjit Sengupta told reporters.

Sengupta, an Awami MP and parliamentary affairs adviser to the prime minister, said "the charges made by the BNP are just imaginary and unfounded. They are trying to make an issue to confront the government."
"The government is aware of the situation. The BNP has been trying to obstruct the business of the legislature...but are very alert," he said.
The BNP lost to the Awami league in a general election held on June 12 under a neutral caretaker government, and billed free and peaceful by local and international monitors.
But Khaleda never accepted the results, which she says had been manipulated to ensure the Awami League's return to power after 21 years.
BNP leaders, including Khaleda, criticised Chief Election Commissioner Abu Hena and President Shahabuddin Ahmed for "protecting Awami interests only".
Speaking at a BNP rally in Dhaka on Thursday, Khaleda asked Bangladeshis to prepare for a campaign to oust Hasina's four-month-old government.
Hasina has kept quiet, except for telling parliament that the BNP was "inciting the armed forces to revolt and even threatening to kill me."
Political analysts said on Sunday the BNP was clearly trying to upset political stability and scare away foreign investors.
